records.name: All Clear
records.skill_description: A frontal sweeping Strike attack that can negate Ki Waves and can be used while guarding.
records.mechanics_notes: Research corpus reports approximately 100 Ki and community-measured damage around 10%. Its defensive properties—Ki Wave negation and guard use—are the primary mechanics; exact current damage and timing remain partially verified.
records.combo_notes: Primarily a defensive utility tool rather than a conventional combo starter; the sweep can create space after guard pressure.
records.pve_notes: Useful against enemies relying on Ki Wave pressure and for creating room when surrounded.
records.pvp_notes: Can answer predictable Ki Wave pressure and convert guarding into a counterattack, but has limited value against pure close-range strike pressure.

records.name: Angry Explosion
records.unlock_method: Expert Mission 12; research corpus reports reward slots associated with Ultimate Finish, with TP Medal Shop rotations also reported
records.source_quest_or_shop: Expert Mission 12 "Attack of the Lone Supersoldier" / TP Medal Shop rotations
records.skill_description: Creates an omnidirectional explosion around the user and can be held to consume additional Ki and prolong the attack.
records.mechanics_notes: The base activation costs 300 Ki. Holding the attack extends the explosion while consuming remaining Ki. Research corpus reports roughly 13 base hits and community damage measurements, but exact current multipliers are not independently reconciled.
records.combo_notes: Best set up after a knockdown or stamina break because of its close range and startup; extended duration can convert remaining Ki into additional hits.
records.pve_notes: The area effect can cover groups and prolonged engagements, especially when targets are confined or unable to escape the radius.
records.pvp_notes: Requires reliable setup because opponents can leave the point-blank radius during startup; extended versions commit substantial Ki.

records.name: Angry Hit
records.skill_description: A charge attack that closes distance by disappearing and reappearing in front of the opponent for a heavy punch.
records.mechanics_notes: The research corpus reports no Ki cost and substantial stamina damage, making the move primarily a stamina-pressure tool. Exact raw damage and timing are not independently verified.
records.combo_notes: The teleporting approach can connect after suitable confirms, but the single-hit structure and readable startup allow prepared opponents to evade.
records.pve_notes: Can help close distance and pressure stamina-heavy AI targets without consuming Ki.
records.pvp_notes: Useful as a surprise gap-closer and stamina-pressure option, but predictable use can be answered by a vanish or defensive reaction.

records.name: Angry Shout
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 68; research corpus reports a reward chance tied to Ultimate Finish and TP Medal Shop rotations
records.source_quest_or_shop: Parallel Quest 68 "Old Rivals and Dragon Balls" / TP Medal Shop rotations
records.skill_description: A radial shockwave evasive that knocks nearby attackers away and restores Ki on use.
records.mechanics_notes: The research corpus reports the standard 300-stamina evasive cost and a Ki refund. The exact amount of restored Ki and damage are not independently verified.
records.combo_notes: Primarily an escape; the radial knockback can create enough separation to reset neutral or prepare a ranged follow-up.
records.pve_notes: Useful when surrounded and valuable for builds that need to recover Ki while escaping pressure.
records.pvp_notes: The Ki refund can improve resource economy, but the activation is still a defensive evasive and should be timed around incoming pressure.

records.name: Burst Blitz
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 178 "The Tireless Pursuit of Strength"
records.source_quest_or_shop: PQ 178; research corpus reports a 50% Ultimate Finish bonus-slot reward
records.skill_description: Teleports behind the opponent and, on a successful hit, automatically continues through multiple follow-ups before finishing with a jump kick.
records.mechanics_notes: The research corpus reports a 300-Ki cost and fixed behind-the-target teleport. Exact hit count and damage multiplier are not independently verified.
records.combo_notes: Best used when the target is vulnerable to a teleport confirm; the automatic follow-up sequence rewards a clean opener but a failed approach wastes the Ki investment.
records.pve_notes: The behind-target delivery can reliably pressure AI that guards forward, while the automatic follow-up sequence provides concentrated single-target damage.
records.pvp_notes: The rear teleport changes the defensive response compared with frontal attacks, but reactive evasives and movement can still counter a predictable cast.
